scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Your watch shows your heart rate, without touching your chest. How does a light know your pulse?

scenes.name: led
scenes.text: Flip the watch over. Those green LEDs shine light into the skin on your wrist.

scenes.name: blood
scenes.text: Blood is red, so it absorbs green light well. More blood means more green light absorbed.

scenes.name: beat
scenes.text: With every heartbeat, a pulse of blood swells the vessels, then it drops. So the absorbed light rises and falls.

scenes.name: sensor
scenes.text: A sensor beside the LEDs measures the light bouncing back. That makes a wave, one bump per beat.

scenes.name: count
scenes.text: Software counts the bumps per minute, and uses the motion sensor to filter out wrist movement.

scenes.name: limits
scenes.text: A loose strap, tattoos, or hard workouts can throw it off. Chest straps are usually more accurate.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Light, blood, bumps, beats. Your pulse, in green. Follow for more on how things really work.
